description: Both are injection-class attacks: untrusted input alters the interpreter's (or model's) intended behavior instead of being treated as inert data.
LLM05 is effectively injection at the output boundary: unsanitized model output reaching a downstream interpreter (shell, query, DOM) the same way unsanitized user input does in classic injection.
Both describe compromise via a third-party dependency the application did not fully vet — a library in A06, a pretrained model/dataset/adapter in LLM03.
Both concern granting more scope or permission than a task requires: object-level in A01 (broken access control), tool/action-level in LLM06 (excessive agentic autonomy).
